issues.legal_issue: The High Court’s supervisory jurisdiction does not permit it to set aside concurrent factual findings merely by reweighing the facts when the subordinate authorities acted within their authority.
material_facts: The Collector found that the commercial plot had been substantially undervalued in the registered instrument and ordered payment of deficient stamp duty; the Commissioner upheld that order.
The High Court, exercising supervisory jurisdiction, set aside those concurrent findings, relying in part on the civil decree for specific performance and presuming the stated sale price was genuine.
The Supreme Court found no basis for the High Court’s interference with the authorities’ findings.
issues.conclusion: The High Court exceeded the limits of its supervisory jurisdiction by disturbing concurrent factual findings without a demonstrated jurisdictional failure or comparable ground for intervention.
issues.legal_principle: Article 227 of the Constitution confers supervisory, not appellate, jurisdiction. It is limited to ensuring that subordinate courts and tribunals act within their authority; it does not permit reappreciation of evidence or correction of ordinary errors of fact. Interference is restricted to cases involving grave dereliction of duty or flagrant abuse of fundamental principles of law or justice. The Court relied on Nagendra Nath Bora v. Commissioner of Hills Division and Appeals, Assam, Nibaran Chandra Bag v. Mahendra Nath Ghughu, Mohd. Yunus v. Mohd. Mustaqim, Laxmikant Revchand Bhojwani v. Pratapsing Mohansingh Pardeshi, Rena Drego v. Lalchand Soni, and Virendra Kashinath Ravat v. Vinayak N. Joshi.

rule.if: high_court_supervisory_review and concurrent_findings and factual_reassessment and subordinate_authorities_within_authority and not grave_dereliction_or_fundamental_abuse

predicates.high_court_supervisory_review: The High Court reviewed decisions of subordinate courts or authorities in the exercise of supervisory jurisdiction.
predicates.concurrent_findings: The subordinate decision-makers reached the same findings on the material facts.
predicates.factual_reassessment: The High Court reassessed the evidence or substituted its view of the facts for the concurrent findings.
predicates.subordinate_authorities_within_authority: The subordinate decision-makers acted within the bounds of their authority.
predicates.grave_dereliction_or_fundamental_abuse: The subordinate decision-makers committed a grave dereliction of duty or a flagrant abuse of fundamental principles of law or justice.

issues.definition: When a High Court exercising supervisory jurisdiction reassesses concurrent findings despite the subordinate authorities acting within their authority and without grave dereliction or fundamental abuse, supervisory interference is unwarranted.

issues.legal_issue: A civil decree for specific performance between private parties does not prevent stamp authorities from determining that a registered transfer instrument understates the property’s value or consideration and recovering deficient stamp duty.
material_facts: The buyer obtained a decree for specific performance in a suit to which the stamp authorities were not parties, and the decree led to registration of a sale deed.
The plot was commercial, and its notified collector rate was substantially higher than the value stated in the registered instrument.

The Collector found that the commercial nature and true value had not been disclosed, determined the deficient duty after proceedings under the applicable undervaluation procedure, and ordered its recovery; the Commissioner upheld that order.
The High Court set aside the authorities’ orders on the basis that the civil decree supported the genuineness of the stated sale price.
issues.conclusion: The civil decree did not require the stamp authorities to presume the stated sale price genuine or prevent them from determining and recovering deficient duty. The Collector’s order, as upheld by the Commissioner, was restored.
issues.legal_principle: Under section 47-A(1)–(3) of the applicable Haryana stamp law, a registering officer who has reason to believe that value or consideration has not been truly stated may refer the instrument to the Collector; the Collector may determine value and duty after a reasonable opportunity to be heard and an inquiry, and any deficient duty is payable by the person liable for it. The Collector may also examine an instrument within the statutory period in the circumstances specified by the section. On these facts, the notified collector rate and the finding that the commercial property had been undervalued supported the determination; a decree in litigation between private parties, to which the State was not a party, did not make the stated price immune from examination.

predicates.registered_property_transfer: A document transferring property was registered and stated a value or consideration for the transfer.
predicates.authority_found_understatement_after_inq: The responsible authority found, after an inquiry, that the value or consideration stated in the instrument was understated.
predicates.property_value_materially_exceeded_state: The value used by the authority for the property was materially higher than the value stated in the instrument.
predicates.decree_suit_excluded_stamp_authorities: A decree relied on to support the stated consideration arose from a suit in which the stamp authorities were not parties.

issues.definition: When a registered property transfer is found after inquiry to be materially understated, and the stamp authorities were not parties to the decree relied on to support the stated value, deficient stamp duty is recoverable.
